## From survey data to structural models

Point clouds, CT scans and photogrammetric surveys describe *what a structure looks
like*, not *how it behaves*. Bridging the two requires meshing strategies that tolerate
noise, occlusions and non-manifold geometry.

- Automatic voxel- and slice-based mesh generation from unstructured 3D data
- Registration and clustering of large point clouds
- Ontology-driven organisation of digital-twin data
- CT-based characterisation of small-scale and biological materials

## Masonry and historical constructions

Masonry is discontinuous, anisotropic and history-dependent. I work on models that keep
the texture visible where it matters and homogenise it where it does not.

- Texture-aware modelling of walls and vaults
- Interface and shell-interface formulations for block assemblies
- Damage, plasticity and frost-induced deterioration
- Seismic assessment of towers and monumental buildings

## Numerical methods

- Locking-free shell and beam finite elements
- Virtual element methods (VEM) on general polytopal meshes
- A-priori and a-posteriori error estimation
- Hybrid and physics-informed neural network surrogates

[FEM shell gallery](gallery/2026-02-fem-shell.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}

## Data-driven and explainable modelling

- Machine-learning and statistical models for structural prediction
- Feature-importance and SHAP-based interpretation of monitoring data
- Data-informed calibration of structural models and digital twins

## Multi-physics degradation

- Coupled thermo-hygro-mechanical processes in porous materials
- Salt crystallization and long-term degradation of masonry
- Environmental actions on historical construction materials

## Sustainable and bio-based materials

- Experimental and numerical characterization of eco-sustainable materials
- Recycled and natural aggregates for energy and structural performance
- Hygrothermal and mechanical testing of innovative mortars
